subproblem.title: Fibrewise a.e. constancy gives the product form H(t, α) = slice average
subproblem.statement: Let a, b, c, d ∈ ℝ with c < d, I := (a, b), J := (c, d), and let H : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ be Lebesgue integrable on I × J. Assume that for almost every t ∈ I there is k ∈ ℝ with H(t, α) = k for almost every α ∈ J. Then H(t, α) = (d − c)⁻¹·∫_J H(t, β) dβ for almost every (t, α) ∈ I × J.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (a b c d : ℝ) (H : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ), c < d → IntegrableOn H (Ioo a b ×ˢ Ioo c d) → (∀ᵐ t, t ∈ Ioo a b → ∃ k : ℝ, ∀ᵐ α, α ∈ Ioo c d → H (t, α) = k) → ∀ᵐ p : ℝ × ℝ, p ∈ Ioo a b ×ˢ Ioo c d → H p = (d - c)⁻¹ * ∫ α in Ioo c d, H (p.1, α)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 6 of the parent-supplied proof. Notation: μ := Lebesgue measure restricted to I, ν := Lebesgue measure restricted to J, and h(t) := (d − c)⁻¹·∫_J H(t, β) dβ.
1. Lebesgue measure on ℝ × ℝ is volume.prod volume (Measure.volume_eq_prod), and (vol|I).prod (vol|J) = (vol.prod vol)|_{I×J} (Measure.prod_restrict). So H is integrable, in particular a.e.-strongly measurable, with respect to μ.prod ν. Let H̃ be strongly measurable with H = H̃ (μ.prod ν)-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk, AEStronglyMeasurable.ae_eq_mk).
2. Let h̃(t) := (d − c)⁻¹·∫_J H̃(t, β) dβ = (d − c)⁻¹·∫ H̃(t, β) dν(β). Then h̃ is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right', then multiplication by a constant).
3. Apply Measure.ae_ae_of_ae_prod to H = H̃ (μ.prod ν)-a.e.: for μ-a.e. t, H(t, ·) = H̃(t, ·) ν-a.e. For such t, h(t) = h̃(t) (integral_congr_ae). Thus h = h̃ μ-a.e.
4. Rewrite the hypothesis with ae_restrict_iff' (I and J are measurable): for μ-a.e. t there is k_t with H(t, ·) = k_t ν-a.e. For such t,
   ∫_J H(t, β) dβ = ∫_J k_t dβ = (d − c)·k_t
   (integral_congr_ae, setIntegral_const, Real.volume_Ioo, using d − c > 0). Hence h(t) = k_t, and H(t, α) = h(t) for ν-a.e. α.
5. Combining steps 3 and 4: for μ-a.e. t, for ν-a.e. α, H̃(t, α) = H(t, α) = h(t) = h̃(t).
6. The set E := {p : H̃(p) = h̃(p.1)} is measurable, since H̃ and h̃∘Prod.fst are strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun). By Measure.ae_prod_iff_ae_ae and step 5, H̃(p) = h̃(p.1) for (μ.prod ν)-a.e. p.
7. Prod.fst is quasi-measure-preserving from μ.prod ν to μ (Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_fst, with QuasiMeasurePreserving.ae). So step 3 gives h̃(p.1) = h(p.1) for (μ.prod ν)-a.e. p.
8. By steps 1, 6 and 7, H(p) = H̃(p) = h̃(p.1) = h(p.1) for (μ.prod ν)-a.e. p. Equivalently (ae_restrict_iff' for the measurable set I × J), this holds for Lebesgue-a.e. p in I × J. This is the claim, since h(p.1) = (d − c)⁻¹·∫_J H(p.1, β) dβ. ∎
proof_key_steps: vol|(I×J) = (vol|I).prod(vol|J); choose a strongly measurable H̃ with H̃ = H a.e.
h̃(t) := (d−c)⁻¹∫_J H̃(t,·) is measurable and agrees a.e. with h(t) := (d−c)⁻¹∫_J H(t,·).
For a.e. t the slice equals its constant k_t a.e. on J, and h(t) = k_t because vol J = d − c.
The measurable set {H̃ = h̃∘fst} has a.e.-full sections, so it is conull for the product measure (ae_prod_iff_ae_ae).
Transfer back to H and h via quasiMeasurePreserving_fst.

audit.reason: The measurable-representative argument supplies the measurability required to reverse the iterated almost-everywhere statement. Since c < d, each slice constant equals its stated average. Product Fubini and the projection's null-set preservation transfer the equality back to H.

subproblem.title: A.e. degree-one multiplicative homogeneity forces h(v) = c·v near 1
subproblem.statement: Let 0 < s ≤ 1 and let h : ℝ → ℝ be almost-everywhere strongly measurable on (1 − s, 1 + s). Assume that for every r ∈ ℝ with |r − 1| < s/4, h(ru) = r·h(u) for almost every u ∈ (1 − s/2, 1 + s/2). Then there is c ∈ ℝ with h(v) = c·v for almost every v ∈ (1 − s/8, 1 + s/8).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (s : ℝ) (h : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < s → s ≤ 1 → AEStronglyMeasurable h (volume.restrict (Ioo (1 - s) (1 + s))) → (∀ r : ℝ, |r - 1| < s / 4 → ∀ᵐ u, u ∈ Ioo (1 - s / 2) (1 + s / 2) → h (r * u) = r * h u) → ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ᵐ v, v ∈ Ioo (1 - s / 8) (1 + s / 8) → h v = c * v
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent-supplied proof (s₁ = s/4). Notation: I := (1 − s, 1 + s), I₁ := (1 − s/2, 1 + s/2), R := (1 − s/4, 1 + s/4), I₂ := (1 − s/8, 1 + s/8), I₃ := (1 − s/16, 1 + s/16); vol is Lebesgue measure on ℝ.
0. (Arithmetic.) |r − 1| < s/4 iff r ∈ R, and then r > 1 − s/4 ≥ 3/4 > 0. Let u ∈ I₁ and r ∈ R; all four bounds are positive. So ru > (1 − s/4)(1 − s/2) = 1 − 3s/4 + s²/8 > 1 − s. Also ru < (1 + s/4)(1 + s/2) = 1 + 3s/4 + s²/8 ≤ 1 + 7s/8 < 1 + s, using s² ≤ s. Hence ru ∈ I. Moreover I₃ ⊆ I₂ ⊆ I₁ ⊆ I ⊆ (0, ∞).
1. (Borel version.) h is a.e.-strongly measurable on I, so there is a measurable h̃ : ℝ → ℝ with h = h̃ a.e. on I (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk). The set {v ∈ I : h(v) ≠ h̃(v)} is contained in a measurable null set N.
2. (Transfer to h̃.) Fix r ∈ R. If u ∈ I₁ and h(ru) ≠ h̃(ru), then ru ∈ I by step 0, so ru ∈ N. The set {u : ru ∈ N} has measure |r⁻¹|·vol(N) = 0 (Real.volume_preimage_mul_left). Also h(u) = h̃(u) for a.e. u ∈ I₁ ⊆ I. Combine these with the hypothesis h(ru) = r·h(u) for a.e. u ∈ I₁: then h̃(ru) = r·h̃(u) for a.e. u ∈ I₁.
3. (Quotient.) Let g(v) := h̃(v)/v, a measurable function. For r ∈ R and a.e. u ∈ I₁ (where u > 0 and r > 0), g(ru) = h̃(ru)/(ru) = r·h̃(u)/(ru) = h̃(u)/u = g(u).
4. (Tonelli.) The set E := {(u, r) ∈ ℝ² : g(ru) = g(u)} is measurable, since (u, r) ↦ ru is continuous and g is measurable. By step 3, for every r ∈ R (hence for vol|R-a.e. r), (u, r) ∈ E for vol|I₁-a.e. u. Now:
   - apply Measure.ae_prod_iff_ae_ae to (vol|R).prod(vol|I₁) and the measurable set {(r, u) : (u, r) ∈ E}: a.e. pair lies in it;
   - transport through Prod.swap (Measure.prod_swap: the image of (vol|R).prod(vol|I₁) under swap is (vol|I₁).prod(vol|R));
   - apply Measure.ae_prod_iff_ae_ae again to (vol|I₁).prod(vol|R) and E.
   Conclusion: for vol|I₁-a.e. u, g(ru) = g(u) for vol|R-a.e. r.
5. (Choice of u₀.) I₃ ⊆ I₁ has measure s/8 > 0. So by Measure.exists_mem_of_measure_ne_zero_of_ae (for vol|I₁) there is u₀ ∈ I₃ with the property of step 4. Put c := g(u₀). Then A := {r ∈ R : g(r u₀) ≠ c} is null.
6. (Rescaling.) Note u₀ > 0. Suppose v ∈ (u₀(1 − s/4), u₀(1 + s/4)) and g(v) ≠ c. Then r := v/u₀ = u₀⁻¹·v lies in R and g(r u₀) = g(v) ≠ c. So v lies in the preimage of A under v ↦ u₀⁻¹·v, which is null: its measure is u₀·vol(A) = 0 (Real.volume_preimage_mul_left). Hence g(v) = c for a.e. v ∈ (u₀(1 − s/4), u₀(1 + s/4)).
7. (Containment.) 1 − s/16 < u₀ < 1 + s/16, and all factors are positive. So u₀(1 − s/4) < (1 + s/16)(1 − s/4) = 1 − 3s/16 − s²/64 < 1 − s/8. Also u₀(1 + s/4) > (1 − s/16)(1 + s/4) = 1 + 3s/16 − s²/64 > 1 + s/8, because s²/64 < s/16 for 0 < s ≤ 1. Hence I₂ ⊆ (u₀(1 − s/4), u₀(1 + s/4)).
8. (Conclusion.) For a.e. v ∈ I₂, h(v) = h̃(v) (I₂ ⊆ I, step 1) and g(v) = c (steps 6–7). Since v > 0, h(v) = h̃(v) = v·g(v) = c·v. ∎
proof_key_steps: Arithmetic: |r−1| < s/4 implies r > 0 and r·(1−s/2, 1+s/2) ⊆ (1−s, 1+s).
Pass to a Borel version h̃ (null sets are preserved by u ↦ ru) and set g(v) := h̃(v)/v; for each r, g(ru) = g(u) for a.e. u.
Tonelli on (1−s/2, 1+s/2)×(1−s/4, 1+s/4) swaps the quantifiers: for a.e. u, g(ru) = g(u) for a.e. r.
Pick such u₀ in (1−s/16, 1+s/16); rescaling r ↦ ru₀ gives g = c := g(u₀) a.e. on (u₀(1−s/4), u₀(1+s/4)) ⊇ (1−s/8, 1+s/8).
Hence h(v) = h̃(v) = c·v a.e. on (1−s/8, 1+s/8).

audit.reason: Almost-everywhere strong measurability suffices through the measurable representative and null-set transfers under nonzero scaling. Tonelli correctly exchanges the exceptional-set quantifiers; the chosen u₀ and explicit interval bounds give precisely the s/8 window, including s = 1.

subproblem.title: A distributional scaling identity gives h(ru) = r·h(u) almost everywhere
subproblem.statement: Let a, b, r ∈ ℝ with r > 0, and let h : ℝ → ℝ be integrable on (a, b) and on (ra, rb). Assume ∫_ℝ l(t/r)·h(t) dt = r²·∫_ℝ l(t)·h(t) dt for every l ∈ C¹(ℝ) with tsupport l ⊆ (a, b). Then h(ru) = r·h(u) for almost every u ∈ (a, b).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (a b r : ℝ) (h : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < r → IntegrableOn h (Ioo a b) → IntegrableOn h (Ioo (r * a) (r * b)) → (∀ l : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 l → tsupport l ⊆ Ioo a b → ∫ t, l (t / r) * h t = r ^ 2 * ∫ t, l t * h t) → ∀ᵐ u, u ∈ Ioo a b → h (r * u) = r * h u
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the second half of step 7 of the parent-supplied proof, in general form. Write J := (a, b).
1. (Change of variables.) For any l : ℝ → ℝ, apply Mathlib Measure.integral_comp_mul_left to G(t) := l(t/r)·h(t) and the factor r: ∫ G(r u) du = |r⁻¹|·∫ G(t) dt. Since r u / r = u (r ≠ 0) and |r⁻¹| = r⁻¹ (r > 0), this reads ∫ l(u)h(ru) du = r⁻¹·∫ l(t/r)h(t) dt. Equivalently, ∫ l(t/r)h(t) dt = r·∫ l(u)h(ru) du. This identity needs no integrability.
2. (Integrability.) h₁ := 1_{(ra,rb)}·h is integrable on ℝ (IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator). Hence u ↦ h₁(ru) is integrable on ℝ (Integrable.comp_mul_left', r ≠ 0). For u ∈ J we have ru ∈ (ra, rb) because r > 0, so h₁(ru) = h(ru). Thus u ↦ h(ru) is integrable on J, and h is integrable on J by hypothesis. Consequently F(u) := h(ru) − r·h(u) is integrable on J, hence locally integrable on the open set J. If l is continuous with tsupport l ⊆ J, then l is bounded (compact support) and vanishes off J. So u ↦ l(u)h(ru) and u ↦ l(u)h(u) are integrable on ℝ (Integrable.bdd_mul applied to the integrable functions 1_J·h(r·) and 1_J·h).
3. (Identity.) Let l ∈ C¹ with tsupport l ⊆ J. By step 1 and the hypothesis, r·∫ l(u)h(ru) du = r²·∫ l(u)h(u) du. Dividing by r > 0 gives ∫ l(u)h(ru) du = r·∫ l(u)h(u) du. By linearity (the integrals are finite by step 2), ∫ l(u)·F(u) du = 0.
4. (Fundamental lemma.) Every l ∈ C^∞(ℝ) with compact support and tsupport l ⊆ J is C¹ (ContDiff.of_le). So ∫ l(u)•F(u) du = 0 for all such l by step 3. By IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero (U := J, F locally integrable on J), F(u) = 0, i.e. h(ru) = r·h(u), for almost every u ∈ J. ∎
proof_key_steps: Change of variables t = ru (Measure.integral_comp_mul_left): ∫ l(t/r)h(t)dt = r∫ l(u)h(ru)du.
u ↦ h(ru) is integrable on (a,b) (Integrable.comp_mul_left' applied to 1_{(ra,rb)}h), so F(u) := h(ru) − r h(u) is integrable on (a,b).
Hence ∫ l(u)F(u)du = 0 for every C¹ l supported in (a,b).
The fundamental lemma on (a,b) gives h(ru) = r h(u) a.e.

audit.reason: Positive r justifies the change of variables and cancellation. Both interval-integrability hypotheses are correctly used to justify the tested difference and integral linearity. The fundamental lemma yields the exact almost-everywhere scaling conclusion.

subproblem.title: The antiderivative of a mean-zero continuous test function is a C¹ test function
subproblem.statement: Let c, d ∈ ℝ and let g : ℝ → ℝ be continuous with tsupport g ⊆ (c, d) and ∫_ℝ g = 0. Then there is ψ : ℝ → ℝ of class C¹ with tsupport ψ ⊆ (c, d) and deriv ψ = g (equality of functions).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (c d : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ), Continuous g → tsupport g ⊆ Ioo c d → ∫ α, g α = 0 → ∃ ψ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ ∧ tsupport ψ ⊆ Ioo c d ∧ deriv ψ = g
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. tsupport g is closed and contained in (c, d) ⊆ [c, d], so it is compact. Thus g is continuous with compact support, hence integrable on ℝ and interval integrable on every bounded interval.
2. If tsupport g = ∅, then g = 0 everywhere and ψ := 0 works: it is C¹, tsupport ψ = ∅, and deriv ψ = 0 = g. Otherwise let p := sInf (tsupport g) and q := sSup (tsupport g). Both belong to the nonempty compact set tsupport g (IsCompact.sInf_mem, IsCompact.sSup_mem), so c < p ≤ q < d. Moreover g(α) = 0 for every α ∉ [p, q], since such α lies outside tsupport g (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
3. Define ψ(x) := ∫_c^x g(α) dα (interval integral). g is continuous and interval integrable (step 1). The fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right, using continuity of g at x) gives HasDerivAt ψ (g x) x for every x ∈ ℝ. Hence ψ is differentiable and deriv ψ = g (HasDerivAt.deriv and function extensionality).
4. ψ is C¹. By contDiff_one_iff_deriv it suffices that ψ is differentiable and that deriv ψ = g is continuous; both hold by step 3.
5. Let x < p. The closed interval between c and x lies in (−∞, p), because c < p and x < p. Since g vanishes there, ψ(x) = 0.
   Now let x > q. Then c < p ≤ q < x and g vanishes outside [p, q] ⊆ (c, x]. Hence ψ(x) = ∫_{(c, x]} g = ∫_ℝ g = 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, and the hypothesis ∫ g = 0). Therefore support ψ ⊆ [p, q].
6. Hence tsupport ψ = closure (support ψ) ⊆ [p, q] ⊆ (c, d). Together with steps 3–4 this proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport g is compact, so g is integrable; if it is empty take ψ = 0, otherwise let p = min tsupport g and q = max tsupport g, with c < p ≤ q < d.
ψ(x) := ∫_c^x g; FTC for continuous g gives deriv ψ = g everywhere, so ψ ∈ C¹.
ψ = 0 on (−∞, p), and ψ(x) = ∫g = 0 for x > q, so tsupport ψ ⊆ [p, q] ⊆ (c, d).

audit.reason: The proof handles empty support, so no additional c < d hypothesis is needed. Otherwise compact support provides interior endpoints; FTC gives deriv ψ = g everywhere, and the zero integral forces the primitive to vanish beyond its support. This proves the exact C¹ and tsupport conclusions.

subproblem.title: A countable family of C¹ test functions separating integrable functions on an interval
subproblem.statement: For all real numbers c, d there is a sequence (F_n)_{n∈ℕ} of C¹ functions ℝ → ℝ with tsupport F_n ⊆ (c, d) for every n, with the following property: every function w : ℝ → ℝ that is integrable on (c, d) and satisfies ∫_ℝ F_n(α)·w(α) dα = 0 for all n vanishes almost everywhere on (c, d).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ c d : ℝ, ∃ F : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ, (∀ n, ContDiff ℝ 1 (F n)) ∧ (∀ n, tsupport (F n) ⊆ Ioo c d) ∧ ∀ w : ℝ → ℝ, IntegrableOn w (Ioo c d) → (∀ n, ∫ α, F n α * w α = 0) → ∀ᵐ α, α ∈ Ioo c d → w α = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Role: this replaces step 3 of the parent-supplied proof, which uses separability of C([−s, s]) via ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace; that instance is not in the import closure of GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean.
0. If d ≤ c then (c, d) = ∅. Take F_n := 0, which is C¹ with empty tsupport; the conclusion is vacuous. From now on assume c < d and write J := (c, d).
1. (Plateau functions.) Let σ := Real.smoothTransition: C^∞, 0 ≤ σ ≤ 1, σ = 0 on (−∞, 0] and σ = 1 on [1, ∞). For p < q and k ∈ ℕ put χ_{p,q,k}(α) := σ(k(α − p))·σ(k(q − α)). Then:
   - χ_{p,q,k} is C^∞, hence C¹, and 0 ≤ χ_{p,q,k} ≤ 1.
   - χ_{p,q,k}(α) = 0 unless p < α < q (if α ≤ p the first argument is ≤ 0; if α ≥ q the second is), so tsupport χ_{p,q,k} ⊆ [p, q].
   - χ_{p,q,k}(α) → 1_{(p,q)}(α) as k → ∞, for every α. If p < α < q, both arguments are ≥ 1 once k ≥ 1/(α − p) and k ≥ 1/(q − α), so the value is eventually 1. Otherwise the value is 0 for every k.
2. (Enumeration.) ℚ × ℚ × ℕ is countable and nonempty, so there is a surjection e : ℕ → ℚ × ℚ × ℕ (exists_surjective_nat). Define F_n := χ_{p,q,k} if e(n) = (p, q, k) with c < p < q < d, and F_n := 0 otherwise. Every F_n is C¹, and tsupport F_n ⊆ [p, q] ⊆ J or tsupport F_n = ∅.
3. (Rational intervals.) Let w be integrable on J with ∫ F_n w = 0 for all n, and let w̄ := 1_J·w; it is integrable on ℝ (IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator). Fix rationals c < p < q < d. For each k choose n with e(n) = (p, q, k). Then ∫ χ_{p,q,k}·w̄ = ∫ F_n·w = 0; the two integrands coincide because χ_{p,q,k} vanishes off J. The functions χ_{p,q,k}·w̄ are dominated by |w̄| and converge pointwise to 1_{(p,q)}·w̄ (step 1). By dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence), ∫_{(p,q)} w̄ = lim_k ∫ χ_{p,q,k}·w̄ = 0.
4. (Primitive.) Let W(x) := ∫_c^x w̄ (interval integral). W is continuous on ℝ (intervalIntegral.continuous_primitive, since w̄ is integrable) and W(c) = 0. For rationals c < p < q < d:
   W(q) − W(p) = ∫_p^q w̄ = ∫_{(p,q]} w̄ = ∫_{(p,q)} w̄ = 0
   (intervalIntegral.integral_interval_sub_left, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, step 3).
   Fix a rational q₀ ∈ J (exists_rat_btwn). Then W = W(q₀) on ℚ ∩ J. The closure of ℚ ∩ J contains [c, d], because between any two reals there is a rational. By continuity W = W(q₀) on [c, d] (Set.EqOn.of_subset_closure). Evaluating at c gives W ≡ 0 on [c, d].
5. (Lebesgue differentiation.) Lebesgue measure on ℝ is uniformly locally doubling (the instance IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure (volume : Measure ℝ) is available). Apply Mathlib IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average to the locally integrable w̄, with K := 1, the constant centre x and radius ρ, along the filter 𝓝[>] 0; note x ∈ closedBall x (1·ρ) for ρ > 0. It gives: for a.e. x ∈ ℝ, the averages ⨍_{closedBall x ρ} w̄ converge to w̄(x) as ρ → 0⁺. Let x ∈ J be such a point. For 0 < ρ < min(x − c, d − x):
   - closedBall x ρ = [x − ρ, x + ρ] ⊆ [c, d] (Real.closedBall_eq_Icc);
   - ∫_{[x−ρ, x+ρ]} w̄ = W(x + ρ) − W(x − ρ) = 0 (integral_Icc_eq_integral_Ioc and step 4);
   - so the average vanishes (setAverage_eq).
   Hence w(x) = w̄(x) = lim 0 = 0. Therefore w = 0 almost everywhere on J. ∎
(An equivalent finish to step 5: since w̄ = 0 off J, W ≡ 0 on all of ℝ. So the finite measures with densities w̄⁺ and w̄⁻ agree on every interval (a', b'] and on ℝ. Measure.ext_of_Ioc_finite then gives equality of these measures, whence w̄ = 0 a.e.)
proof_key_steps: Smooth plateaus χ_{p,q,k}(α) = σ(k(α−p))σ(k(q−α)) are C¹, supported in [p,q], bounded by 1, and converge pointwise to 1_{(p,q)}.
Enumerate the rational triples (p,q,k) with c<p<q<d by a surjection ℕ → ℚ×ℚ×ℕ to define F_n.
Dominated convergence gives ∫_{(p,q)} w = 0 for all rational c<p<q<d.
The continuous primitive W of 1_J·w is constant on ℚ∩J, hence W ≡ 0 on [c,d].
Lebesgue differentiation (IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average) gives w = 0 a.e. on (c,d).

audit.reason: The supplied proof completely constructs the sequence, including empty intervals and invalid enumeration entries. Dominated convergence gives vanishing rational-interval integrals; continuity of the primitive and Lebesgue differentiation establish the exact separating property without circular reliance.

subproblem.title: Normalized C¹ bump supported in a given open interval
subproblem.statement: For real numbers c < d there is a function χ : ℝ → ℝ of class C¹ such that tsupport χ ⊆ (c, d) and ∫_ℝ χ(α) dα = 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ c d : ℝ, c < d → ∃ χ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 χ ∧ tsupport χ ⊆ Ioo c d ∧ ∫ α, χ α = 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context: Mathlib's normalized bump API (ContDiffBump.normed, ContDiffBump.integral_normed) is not in the import closure of GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean, so the bump is built by hand. This exact construction was kernel-checked during the decomposition review.
1. Let σ := Real.smoothTransition. Then σ is C^∞ (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff), 0 ≤ σ ≤ 1 (Real.smoothTransition.nonneg, Real.smoothTransition.le_one), σ(x) = 0 for x ≤ 0 (zero_of_nonpos) and σ(x) = 1 for x ≥ 1 (one_of_one_le).
2. Put m := (c + d)/2, ρ := (d − c)/2 > 0, p := m − ρ/2 and q := m + ρ/2, so that c < p < q < d. Define θ(α) := σ((4/ρ)(α − p)) · σ((4/ρ)(q − α)). Each factor is σ composed with an affine map, so θ is C^∞, in particular C¹. Also θ ≥ 0.
3. If α < p then (4/ρ)(α − p) ≤ 0, so the first factor is 0. If α > q then (4/ρ)(q − α) ≤ 0, so the second factor is 0. Hence support θ ⊆ [p, q]. Since [p, q] is closed, tsupport θ ⊆ [p, q] ⊆ (c, d). In particular tsupport θ is a closed subset of the compact interval [c, d], so θ has compact support.
4. At α = m both arguments equal (4/ρ)(ρ/2) = 2 ≥ 1, so θ(m) = 1 ≠ 0.
5. θ is continuous, compactly supported, nonnegative and not identically zero. Hence I_θ := ∫_ℝ θ > 0 (Mathlib Continuous.integral_pos_of_hasCompactSupport_nonneg_nonzero).
6. Let χ := I_θ⁻¹ · θ. Then χ is C¹, being a constant times a C¹ function. Also tsupport χ ⊆ tsupport θ ⊆ (c, d) (tsupport_mul_subset_right). Finally ∫ χ = I_θ⁻¹ · I_θ = 1 (integral_const_mul). ∎
proof_key_steps: Build θ(α) = σ((4/ρ)(α − p))·σ((4/ρ)(q − α)) from σ = Real.smoothTransition, with c < p < q < d.
θ is C^∞ and ≥ 0, and vanishes off [p, q], so tsupport θ ⊆ (c, d); also θ((c+d)/2) = 1.
∫θ > 0, since θ is continuous, compactly supported, nonnegative and nonzero.
Normalize: χ := (∫θ)⁻¹·θ is C¹, keeps the support, and has ∫χ = 1.

subproblem.title: Reduction of a product-tested integral of a product-form density to one variable
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (a b c d : ℝ) (H : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ) (h f ψ₀ : ℝ → ℝ), (∀ᵐ p : ℝ × ℝ, p ∈ Ioo a b ×ˢ Ioo c d → H p = h p.1) → (∀ t, t ∉ Ioo a b → f t = 0) → (∀ α, α ∉ Ioo c d → ψ₀ α = 0) → ∫ α, ψ₀ α = 1 → ∫ p : ℝ × ℝ, f p.1 * ψ₀ p.2 * H p = ∫ t, f t * h t
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the first half of step 7 of the parent-supplied proof, in general form. This proof was kernel-checked during the decomposition review. Write O := (a, b) × (c, d), a measurable set.
1. Let p ∉ O. Either p.1 ∉ (a, b), so f(p.1) = 0, or p.2 ∉ (c, d), so ψ₀(p.2) = 0. Hence f(p.1)ψ₀(p.2)H(p) = 0 off O, and ∫_{ℝ²} f(p.1)ψ₀(p.2)H(p) dp = ∫_O f(p.1)ψ₀(p.2)H(p) dp (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
2. By hypothesis, f(p.1)ψ₀(p.2)H(p) = (f(p.1)·h(p.1))·ψ₀(p.2) for a.e. p ∈ O. So the two set integrals over O agree (setIntegral_congr_ae, O measurable).
3. Lebesgue measure on ℝ² is volume.prod volume (Measure.volume_eq_prod). Apply setIntegral_prod_mul to the functions t ↦ f(t)h(t) and ψ₀; this identity holds without any integrability assumption. It gives ∫_O (f h)(p.1)·ψ₀(p.2) dp = (∫_{(a,b)} f(t)h(t) dt)·(∫_{(c,d)} ψ₀(α) dα).
4. ψ₀ = 0 off (c, d), so ∫_{(c,d)} ψ₀ = ∫_ℝ ψ₀ = 1. Likewise f·h = 0 off (a, b), so ∫_{(a,b)} f h = ∫_ℝ f h (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). Combining steps 1–4 gives ∫_{ℝ²} f(p.1)ψ₀(p.2)H(p) dp = ∫_ℝ f(t)h(t) dt. ∎
proof_key_steps: The integrand vanishes off (a,b)×(c,d), so the integral equals the set integral over the box.
On the box, replace H(p) by h(p.1) a.e. (setIntegral_congr_ae).
setIntegral_prod_mul factors the box integral as (∫_{(a,b)} f h)·(∫_{(c,d)} ψ₀), with no integrability needed.
Both factors are whole-line integrals because f·h and ψ₀ vanish off the intervals; ∫ψ₀ = 1.

subproblem.title: Fubini and the fundamental lemma: product-tested vanishing forces a.e. vanishing of slice integrals
subproblem.statement: Let a, b, c, d ∈ ℝ, I := (a, b), J := (c, d), and let H : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ be Lebesgue integrable on I × J. Let g : ℝ → ℝ be continuous with tsupport g ⊆ J. Assume ∫_{ℝ×ℝ} g(α)·l(t)·H(t, α) d(t, α) = 0 for every l ∈ C¹(ℝ) with tsupport l ⊆ I. Then ∫_J g(α)·H(t, α) dα = 0 for almost every t ∈ I.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (a b c d : ℝ) (H : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ), IntegrableOn H (Ioo a b ×ˢ Ioo c d) → Continuous g → tsupport g ⊆ Ioo c d → (∀ l : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 l → tsupport l ⊆ Ioo a b → ∫ p : ℝ × ℝ, g p.2 * l p.1 * H p = 0) → ∀ᵐ t, t ∈ Ioo a b → ∫ α in Ioo c d, g α * H (t, α) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent-supplied proof (with g := ψ'). Notation: μ := Lebesgue measure restricted to I, and ν := Lebesgue measure restricted to J.
1. Lebesgue measure on ℝ × ℝ is volume.prod volume (Measure.volume_eq_prod), and (vol|I).prod (vol|J) = (vol.prod vol)|_{I×J} (Measure.prod_restrict). Hence H is integrable with respect to μ.prod ν.
2. tsupport g is closed and contained in [c, d], so it is compact. A continuous compactly supported function is bounded, so |g| ≤ M for some M (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). Therefore K(t, α) := g(α)·H(t, α) is integrable w.r.t. μ.prod ν (Integrable.bdd_mul; p ↦ g(p.2) is continuous, hence a.e.-strongly measurable).
3. Put Φ(t) := ∫_J g(α) H(t, α) dα = ∫ K(t, α) dν(α). By Fubini (Integrable.integral_prod_left), Φ is μ-integrable, i.e. integrable on I. In particular Φ is locally integrable on the open set I.
4. Let l ∈ C¹(ℝ) with tsupport l ⊆ I. Then l is continuous with compact support (a closed subset of [a, b]), hence bounded, and l(t) = 0 for t ∉ I. The integrand F(p) := g(p.2)·l(p.1)·H(p) vanishes for p ∉ I × J: if p.1 ∉ I then l(p.1) = 0, and if p.2 ∉ J then g(p.2) = 0. Therefore:
   ∫_{ℝ²} F = ∫_{I×J} F (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero)
   = ∫ l(p.1)·K(p) d(μ.prod ν)(p)
   = ∫_I l(t) (∫_J K(t, α) dα) dt (integral_prod; the integrand is a bounded measurable function times an integrable one, hence integrable; then integral_const_mul in the inner integral)
   = ∫_I l(t) Φ(t) dt = ∫_ℝ l(t) Φ(t) dt (l vanishes off I).
   By hypothesis ∫_{ℝ²} F = 0, so ∫_ℝ l(t) Φ(t) dt = 0.
5. Every l ∈ C^∞(ℝ) with compact support and tsupport l ⊆ I is C¹ (ContDiff.of_le). So by step 4, ∫_ℝ l(t)·Φ(t) dt = 0 for all such l. Apply the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations on an open set (Mathlib IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero with U := I and f := Φ, which is locally integrable on I by step 3). It gives Φ(t) = 0 for almost every t ∈ I, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: vol|(I×J) = (vol|I).prod(vol|J); g is bounded, so g(α)H(t,α) is integrable on the product.
Φ(t) := ∫_J g(α)H(t,α)dα is integrable on I (Fubini).
The test integrand vanishes off I×J, so Fubini turns the hypothesis into ∫ l(t)Φ(t)dt = 0 for every C¹ l with tsupport in I.
The fundamental lemma on the open interval I gives Φ = 0 a.e. on I.

subproblem.title: Vanishing product-tested α-derivative forces a.e. constant slices (fibrewise du Bois-Reymond)
subproblem.statement: Let a, b, c, d ∈ ℝ with c < d, I := (a, b), J := (c, d), and let H : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ be Lebesgue integrable on I × J. Assume ∫_{ℝ×ℝ} ψ'(α)·l(t)·H(t, α) d(t, α) = 0 for all ψ, l ∈ C¹(ℝ) with tsupport ψ ⊆ J and tsupport l ⊆ I, where ψ' = deriv ψ. Then for almost every t ∈ I there is k ∈ ℝ with H(t, α) = k for almost every α ∈ J.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–5 of the parent-supplied proof. Two citations there are not in the import closure of GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean and are replaced:
- the separability step, by the countable family of countable_separating_tests;
- the SimonGMT Chapter08 constancy lemma, by that family's separating property.
This argument was kernel-checked during the review as a hypothesis-only assembly from the four sibling statements.
1. By normalized_bump (Submission.idtp_cse_ah_normalized_bump, using c < d), fix χ ∈ C¹ with tsupport χ ⊆ J and ∫χ = 1. By countable_separating_tests (Submission.idtp_cse_ah_countable_separating_tests), fix C¹ functions F_n (n ∈ ℕ) with tsupport F_n ⊆ J such that every w integrable on J with ∫ F_n w = 0 for all n vanishes a.e. on J. The tsupports of χ and of each F_n are closed subsets of [c, d]. So these functions are continuous with compact support, hence bounded, integrable on ℝ, and zero outside J.
2. For n ∈ ℕ let g_n := F_n − (∫F_n)·χ. Then:
   - g_n is continuous;
   - tsupport g_n ⊆ tsupport F_n ∪ tsupport χ ⊆ J (tsupport_sub, tsupport_mul_subset_right);
   - ∫ g_n = ∫F_n − (∫F_n)·1 = 0 (integral_sub, integral_const_mul).
   By antiderivative_test (Submission.idtp_cse_ah_antiderivative_test) there is ψ_n ∈ C¹ with tsupport ψ_n ⊆ J and deriv ψ_n = g_n.
3. Let l ∈ C¹ with tsupport l ⊆ I. Apply the hypothesis to (ψ_n, l) and rewrite deriv ψ_n = g_n: ∫ g_n(p.2)·l(p.1)·H(p) dp = 0. Hence slice_integral_ae_zero (Submission.idtp_cse_ah_slice_integral_ae_zero, with g := g_n, which is continuous with tsupport in J) gives: for a.e. t ∈ I, ∫_J g_n(α)·H(t, α) dα = 0.
4. H is integrable w.r.t. (vol|I).prod(vol|J) = vol|(I×J) (Measure.prod_restrict, Measure.volume_eq_prod). By Fubini (Integrable.prod_right_ae, rewritten with ae_restrict_iff'), for a.e. t ∈ I the slice α ↦ H(t, α) is integrable on J.
5. A countable union of null sets is null (ae_all_iff). So for a.e. t ∈ I, the slice H(t, ·) is integrable on J and ∫_J g_n(α)·H(t, α) dα = 0 for all n simultaneously. Fix such a t.
6. Put k := ∫_J χ(α)·H(t, α) dα and w(α) := H(t, α) − k. Then w is integrable on J: it is the integrable slice minus a constant on the finite-measure set J. For each n, the products F_n·H(t, ·) and χ·H(t, ·) are integrable on J (bounded continuous times integrable; Integrable.bdd_mul). Since F_n vanishes off J,
   ∫_ℝ F_n w = ∫_J F_n(α)·H(t, α) dα − k·∫_ℝ F_n.
   By step 5 and linearity,
   0 = ∫_J g_n(α)·H(t, α) dα = ∫_J F_n(α)·H(t, α) dα − (∫F_n)·k.
   Subtracting, ∫_ℝ F_n w = 0 for every n.
7. By the separating property of (F_n), w = 0 a.e. on J, i.e. H(t, α) = k for a.e. α ∈ J. Since t was an arbitrary point of a full-measure subset of I, the claim follows. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix a normalized C¹ bump χ in J (normalized_bump) and the countable separating family F_n on J (countable_separating_tests).
g_n := F_n − (∫F_n)χ is continuous, supported in J and mean-zero; antiderivative_test gives ψ_n ∈ C¹ supported in J with ψ_n' = g_n.
The hypothesis with ψ_n and slice_integral_ae_zero give ∫_J g_n H(t,·) = 0 for a.e. t; slices are integrable for a.e. t (Fubini); intersect over n.
For such t, w := H(t,·) − ∫_J χH(t,·) satisfies ∫F_n w = 0 for all n, so w = 0 a.e. on J.
